AetherNova Pharmaceuticals - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AetherNova Pharmaceuticals Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss AetherNova Pharmaceuticals's financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lisa Chen, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer; Jordan Lee, Head of Commercial; and Carlos Ruiz, Head of Manufacturing.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of AetherNova Pharmaceuticals.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. AetherNova Pharmaceuticals delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust revenue growth from our core franchises, accelerating pipeline milestones, and successful new product launches. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives, with a focus on our new product launches and market share gains, which have been a standout this quarter. Thank you, Mike, and good morning, everyone. Today, I'd like to dive deeper into one of the brightest spots in our Q3 results: the accelerating momentum from our new product launches and the resulting market share gains across key franchises. As you know, AetherNova Pharmaceuticals has strategically positioned itself at the intersection of high-growth therapeutic areas—immuno-oncology, cardiometabolic disease, and rare genetic disorders—leveraging our proprietary ADCs, bispecific antibodies, and mRNA platforms. Our launches are not just hitting inflection points; they're reshaping competitive landscapes, with IQVIA MAT data through September showing us capturing over 12% share in targeted segments, up from sub-2% a year ago.

Let me start with our flagship launch, VitaSlim (vitasemaglutide), our once-weekly subcutaneous GLP-1/GIP dual agonist for obesity and type 2 diabetes. Launched in the U.S. in late Q1 following Priority Review approval, VitaSlim generated $285 million in net U.S. sales in Q3—exceeding our guidance by 15% and representing a 180% sequential ramp from Q2's $102 million. This performance is driven by explosive prescription growth: new Rx (NRx) volumes hit 1.2 million in Q3, a 45% month-over-month increase, with total Rx (TRx) reaching 2.8 million—a 320% YoY surge per Symphony Health data. On a moving annual total (MAT) basis, we're now at 4.7% share of the GLP-1 market, up from launch at <1%, steadily eroding share from leaders like Novo Nordisk's Ozempic/Wegovy (down 3 points to 52% combined) and Eli Lilly's Mounjaro/Zepbound (down 2 points to 38%). Refill rates are holding strong at 78% at 90 days, outperforming the class average of 72%, thanks to VitaSlim's differentiated profile: superior weight loss of 22.5% at 72 weeks in our pivotal SURMOUNT-3 trial versus 18-20% for comparators, with 30% fewer GI adverse events.

Regionally, the U.S. remains our powerhouse, accounting for 92% of Q3 sales, bolstered by formulary wins with CVS Caremark (Tier 2 access for 65% of lives) and Express Scripts (preferred status post-rebate negotiations at ~45% WAC). We've locked in $1.2 billion in gross-to-net rebates for 2024, aligning with payer demands while preserving ASP stability at $1,450 per fill. In Europe, EMA approval came in early October, with launches in Germany and the UK underway—early wholesaler data shows 150,000 packs shipped in the first two weeks, targeting 2% EU share by year-end. Asia-Pacific is next: our partnership with Takeda for Japan filing submission in Q4, leveraging their 20,000-salesforce footprint, positions us for $150 million in 2025 royalties. Strategically, we're scaling manufacturing at our North Carolina facility, which ramped 60% capacity in Q3 via single-use bioreactor tech, ensuring supply for 5 million patients annually by 2025. DTC spend hit $120 million in Q3, with "Real Results, Real Life" campaign driving 25% uplift in branded searches versus Keytruda-like awareness benchmarks.

Shifting to immuno-oncology, our VitaCyte-ADX (vitaadc-101), a next-gen antibody-drug conjugate targeting HER2-low breast cancer, launched in Q4 2023 and is firing on all cylinders. Q3 U.S. sales reached $210 million, a 75% YoY increase, with MAT share now at 11.2% in the metastatic breast cancer (mBC) ADC space—gaining 4.5 points from Roche's Kadcyla and Daiichi Sankyo/AstraZeneca's Enhertu. Patient starts grew 35% QoQ to 18,500, fueled by label expansion data from our Phase 3 DESTINY-Breast05 readout: ORR of 68% versus 52% for Enhertu, with median PFS of 15.2 months. We're seeing line-of-therapy shifts, with 40% uptake in second-line settings ahead of Kadcyla.

Internationally, ex-U.S. sales doubled to $45 million, led by Japan (PMDA approval in May) where we're partnering with Eisai for co-promotion, capturing 8% share in a $1.2 billion market. EU rollout expands to France and Italy in Q4 post-CHMP positive opinion. Key initiative here: our "precision payload" tech—topoisomerase-1 inhibitor with a cleavable linker—delivers 2x bystander effect, minimizing off-target toxicity, which resonated at ASCO 2024 with 15 abstracts. Payer traction is robust: 85% Medicare Part D coverage, and we're negotiating value-based agreements tying rebates to PFS milestones, similar to Merck's Keytruda deals.

Finally, early momentum in rare diseases with GeneFix-R (rAAV9-SGCG), our gene therapy for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2D. BLA accepted with Priority Review; launch slated for Q4 2024. Bridge data from our pivotal trial shows 85% dystrophin expression at 52 weeks, positioning us against Sarepta's Elevidys in Duchenne. Pre-launch access programs have enrolled 120 patients, with peak sales potential of $800 million, per Evaluate Pharma consensus.

Overall trends underscore our playbook: launches averaging 150% of Street sales expectations, 10-15% share gains per quarter in addressable markets, and a 25% YoY increase in our top-10 prescribers panel. Risks remain—supply chain pressures from raw material inflation (up 12% YoY) and rebate creep—but our hedges include long-term API contracts and $500 million in FY24 capex for U.S. and Singapore facilities. Strategically, we're layering on combos: VitaSlim + SGLT2 pilots with our partner portfolio, and VitaCyte-ADX + PD-1 data readout in Q4 to defend moats against biosimilars looming in 2028. These launches validate our $15 billion 2028 revenue target, with 60% from new products.

We are particularly excited about AETH-301 and its potential to transform HER2-low breast cancer treatment with superior efficacy and safety.

Now, I will turn the call over to Mike Harlan, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Mike Harlan, CFO:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a solid third quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $2.6 billion, an increase of 14% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by volume growth across our core franchises in oncology, cardiometabolics, and immunology, along with emerging market expansion and new launches.

I'll now turn to our Q3 2024 geographic revenue performance, which underscores the diversification and resilience of our portfolio amid a dynamic global macro environment. Total net product sales reached $2.6 billion, up 14% year-over-year on a reported basis and 16% at constant currency. Starting with the high-level breakdown: The U.S. remains our largest market at 54% of total revenue, or $1.4 billion, reflecting 11% YoY growth. This was propelled by continued momentum in our flagship GLP-1 agonist, NovaGLP, which saw a 22% YoY increase to $850 million, benefiting from expanded label indications for cardiovascular risk reduction and strong uptake in the obesity segment, akin to the dynamics we've seen with peers like Novo Nordisk's Ozempic and Wegovy. Our oncology portfolio, led by the PD-1 inhibitor OncoTarget, contributed $420 million, up 9%, despite some payer pushback on prior authorizations. U.S. growth was volume-led, with average selling prices stable at +1% sequentially, supported by our 340B rebate management and gross-to-net adjustments holding steady at 28%.

Europe accounted for 24% of revenues, or $624 million, growing 6% YoY reported and 9% at CER. Pricing remains challenged by HTA scrutiny and clawbacks in key markets like Germany and France, but volume uptake for NovaGLP in Type 2 diabetes tenders offset this, adding $150 million. Our immunology asset, ImmunoBlock—a BTK inhibitor with best-in-class selectivity—launched successfully in Spain and Italy, capturing early share in the relapsed/refractory CLL space against ibrutinib generics. Japan and established Asia-Pacific markets rounded out 11% at $286 million, up 15% YoY, fueled by reimbursement expansions for OncoTarget in NSCLC and partnerships with local players like Takeda for co-promotion.

Now, shifting to the standout story: emerging markets, which represented 11% of total revenue at $286 million—yes, that's right, matching established Asia-Pacific—and delivered explosive 28% YoY growth at CER, accelerating from 22% in Q2. This segment now contributes over 20% of our ex-U.S. growth, validating our multi-year strategy to tap into underserved patient populations amid rising healthcare access and chronic disease prevalence. Let me break it down regionally.

China led with 42% of emerging market sales, or $120 million, surging 35% YoY following NMPA approval and launch of NovaGLP in March. We're capturing share in a market projected to exceed $10 billion for GLP-1s by 2027, per IQVIA estimates, through our JV with Sinopharm, which enables localized pricing at approximately 60% of U.S. ASPs while maintaining healthy margins via tech transfer for fill-finish manufacturing in Shanghai. Volume exceeded 500,000 units in Q3, driven by Tier-2/3 city hospital tenders and digital patient support programs integrated with WeChat health ecosystems.

Latin America grew 25% to $65 million, with Brazil accounting for 55% of the region via ANVISA-approved tenders for our generic portfolio—post-patent expiry versions of Lipitor-like statins and our biosimilar to adalimumab, NovaHumira—which won 40% market share in public procurement auctions. In Mexico, partnerships with Laboratorios PiSA have ramped OncoTarget access, adding $20 million amid oncology incidence rising 5% annually per GLOBOCAN data.

India contributed $50 million, up 22%, leveraging our Hyderabad facility for API production of small molecules, reducing duties and enabling competitive pricing for CardioShield, our PCSK9 inhibitor biosimilar to Repatha. We've secured 15 state-level MoUs for diabetes screening, aligning with the Ayushman Bharat scheme, which targets 100 million beneficiaries.

The Middle East and Africa (MEA) rounded out at $51 million, +30% YoY, with key wins in Saudi Arabia's SFDA tenders for ImmunoBlock and volume ramps in Egypt and South Africa through named-patient programs. Our patient access initiative, NovaAccess, donated over 50,000 units in Q3, fostering goodwill and pipeline entry for next-gen assets.

Strategically, emerging markets are no longer a footnote—they're a growth engine. We've invested $250 million over the past 18 months in local capabilities: three new fill-finish lines in Brazil and India, AI-driven supply chain optimization to counter FX volatility (e.g., BRL depreciation hedged at 85% efficacy), and over 20 BD deals, including a recent MOU with Dr. Reddy's for biosimilar co-development. Risks remain—regulatory delays in Indonesia and currency headwinds shaved 2 points off growth—but our ex-U.S. tariff exposure is minimal at under 5% of COGS.

Looking forward, we expect emerging markets to grow 25-30% in FY2024, targeting 15% of total revenue by 2026, supported by eight upcoming launches, including our bispecific antibody in China. This diversification de-risks our model against U.S. pricing reforms like the Inflation Reduction Act, while capitalizing on 7%+ global pharma CAGR in EMs per Evaluate Pharma forecasts.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $450 million, or $1.85 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $520 million, or $2.13 per share.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q3 earnings call. Before I dive into the financials, I'd like to spend some time on our business development activities, which continue to be a cornerstone of our strategy at AetherNova Pharmaceuticals. As you know, in the current biotech landscape—marked by elevated interest rates, a more selective capital market, and intensifying competition in high-growth areas like oncology, immunology, and cardiometabolics—we've prioritized value-accretive deals that de-risk our pipeline, expand our modalities, and unlock non-dilutive funding. Over the past quarter, we've executed three transformative transactions totaling approximately $1.2 billion in enterprise value, including upfronts, milestones, and potential royalties. These moves not only bolster our top- and mid-stage pipeline but also position us to capture a larger share of the $1.5 trillion global pharma market projected by IQVIA through 2028.

Let me break this down by category, starting with licensing deals. We've been highly active here, focusing on in-licensing best-in-class assets from emerging biotechs while selectively out-licensing regional rights to monetize our programs efficiently. Our flagship in-licensing deal this quarter was with Apex Oncology, a stealth-stage Cambridge, MA-based company, for their next-generation ADC—antibody-drug conjugate—targeting HER2-low breast cancer. This asset, AOP-301, has demonstrated a 65% ORR in heavily pretreated patients in its Phase 1b/2 trial, with a manageable safety profile outperforming Enhertu in early readouts. We paid a $150 million upfront—fully funded from our $2.8 billion cash position—and assumed $800 million in milestones tied to regulatory and commercial hurdles, plus tiered royalties starting at 18% on net sales, scaling to 25% above $1 billion annually.

Strategically, this fits our push into the $50 billion-plus ADC market, where leaders like Seagen (now Pfizer) and Daiichi Sankyo have set the bar with blockbusters. We're accelerating AOP-301 into a pivotal Phase 3 trial by mid-2025, leveraging our Miami-based CMC expertise to optimize linker-payload chemistry and reduce DLTs. On the out-licensing front, we granted China and Southeast Asia rights for our lead GLP-1/GIP dual agonist, BNT-450—for obesity and NASH—to Hansoh Pharma for $200 million upfront, $450 million in milestones, and double-digit royalties. This de-risks our ex-US exposure in a region growing at 12% CAGR, per Evaluate Pharma, amid China's push for innovative therapies under the NMPA's accelerated pathways. Collectively, these licensing deals add over $3 billion in projected peak sales to our NPV models, with a 2-3 year acceleration to market for two programs.

Turning to acquisitions, we closed our most significant tuck-in to date: the $650 million acquisition of ImmunoForge Biologics, a San Diego-headquartered firm specializing in bispecific T-cell engagers for autoimmune diseases. ImmunoForge brings two Phase 2-ready assets—IF-202 for rheumatoid arthritis and IF-205 for lupus—both engineered with their proprietary "silent Fc" domain to minimize CRS risks, a key differentiator from Regeneron's odronextamab or Xencor's XmAb platforms. The deal structure included $450 million upfront and $200 million contingent on Phase 2 data readouts expected in H2 2025. We anticipate $50 million in near-term R&D synergies by folding their 25-person team into our Redwood City hub and consolidating preclinical manufacturing.

This acquisition addresses a critical gap in our immunology portfolio, where autoimmune therapies are forecasted to exceed $150 billion by 2030, driven by AbbVie's Skyrizi and Humira erosion dynamics. Regionally, it strengthens our EU footprint—ImmunoForge had orphan designations from EMA for both assets—helping navigate the post-Brexit CTIS framework for faster multinational trials. In the U.S., it aligns with FDA's emphasis on patient-centric endpoints like PROs in lupus trials. Post-close, we've initiated a $30 million bridging study combining IF-202 with our JAK inhibitor, targeting a 40% improvement in DAS28 scores. M&A like this reflects broader industry trends: biotech buyouts surged 25% YoY in H1 2024 per PitchBook, with mid-caps like ours pursuing "pipeline tuck-ins" to counter Big Pharma's $200 billion war chest for external innovation.

Finally, partnerships have been our engine for shared-risk advancement. We expanded our strategic alliance with Roche/Genentech, now valued at over $1 billion across three programs. Under the amended agreement, they're co-developing our CRISPR-based base editor, BNT-720, for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia—building on Vertex/CRISPR Therapeutics' Casgevy success but with a 50% lower editing efficiency threshold for outpatient dosing. Roche chipped in $100 million in near-term R&D funding, with opt-in rights for ex-U.S. commercialization and 50/50 profit splits. This partnership mitigates our exposure to the high-cost gene therapy CMC space, where viral vector shortages have delayed 30% of programs industry-wide.

We also inked a manufacturing partnership with Samsung Biologics for our oncology bispecifics, securing 20,000 liters of capacity through 2028 at a blended COGS of $45/g—20% below market amid capacity constraints post-COVID. This ensures supply chain resilience for our U.S. and EU launches, particularly as Japan and Korea ramp up biosimilars pressure. Looking regionally, Asia-Pacific partnerships now represent 35% of our BD activity, up from 20% last year, capitalizing on Singapore's BIOMAP incentives and India's CDMO boom. In contrast, our U.S. focus remains on NIH-funded initiatives like ARPA-H's $1 billion biotech accelerator, while Europe demands more pharmacovigilance commitments under the new Clinical Trials Regulation.

Strategically, these initiatives underscore our "3-3-3" framework: three deals per year, each adding three late-stage programs, targeting three therapeutic franchises. They've diversified our revenue—BD now contributes 15% of pro forma 2025 guidance, up from 8%—while derisking via non-dilutive capital exceeding $500 million YTD. Forward-looking, we're tracking 15 opportunities in our deal funnel, including gene therapy tuck-ins and AI-driven small molecule discovery pacts, with a pipeline NPV uplift of $5.2 billion at a 12% discount rate.

In summary, our business development engine is firing on all cylinders, positioning AetherNova for sustained growth amid a frothy M&A environment.

Our operating expenses were $478 million, reflecting strategic investments in late-stage pipeline advancement offset by efficiency gains. Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining NovaPharm's Q3 earnings call. As we dive into our operating expense analysis, I'll highlight our disciplined approach to capital allocation amid a dynamic biotech landscape marked by escalating R&D intensity, reimbursement headwinds in Europe, and accelerating demand for next-gen modalities like ADCs and bispecific antibodies. For the quarter, total operating expenses came in at $478 million, up 12% year-over-year but flat sequentially from Q2, aligning with the midpoint of our guidance range of $460-490 million. This reflects our strategic investments in a late-stage pipeline while delivering 8% OpEx efficiency gains through targeted cost levers. Excluding $22 million in one-time restructuring charges related to our legacy small-molecule wind-down, adjusted OpEx grew just 9% YoY, underscoring our focus on high-ROI programs.

Let me break this down by category, starting with R&D, which remains the cornerstone of our value creation in this industry. Research and Development Expenses: $295 million, or 62% of total OpEx, up 18% YoY and 5% QoQ. R&D intensity – defined as R&D as a percentage of revenue – stood at 48%, in line with peers like Regeneron and Amgen during their growth phases, but below pure-play biotechs like CRISPR Therapeutics at 75%+. This uptick was driven by three key pillars: 1. Clinical Trial Acceleration (65% of R&D spend): We ramped investments in our flagship NP-401, our next-gen PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody for frontline NSCLC, with Phase 3 enrollment now at 85% complete across 120 global sites. Trial costs hit $110 million this quarter, up 25% YoY, reflecting expanded cohorts in China via our partnership with Sinopharm and topline data readout expected Q1 2025. Similarly, NP-289, our HER2-directed ADC akin to Enhertu's success story, incurred $75 million in manufacturing scale-up and CMC bridging studies for our anticipated BLA filing in H2 2025. 2. Early-Stage Innovation (25% of R&D): $42 million funded AI/ML-driven drug discovery platforms, leveraging tools similar to Exscientia's Centaur Chemist to nominate three new candidates in oncology and rare genetic diseases. This includes our CRISPR-Cas13 collaboration with Beam Therapeutics, where we advanced in vivo editing for DMD, offsetting some costs through $15 million in milestone receipts. 3. Technical and Process Initiatives (10%): We realized $8 million in savings from outsourcing toxicology studies to WuXi AppTec in Asia, reducing U.S.-based GLP spend by 20%, while investing $12 million in mRNA lipid nanoparticle optimization post our COVID lessons learned. Regionally, 55% of R&D was U.S.-centric due to FDA interactions, 25% Europe for EMA alignment on NP-401's superiority claims over Keytruda, and 20% Asia-Pacific, where lower CRO costs (30% below U.S. benchmarks) supported faster patient recruitment amid China's NMPA fast-track for ADCs.

Selling, General & Administrative Expenses: $162 million, or 34% of total OpEx, flat YoY and down 3% QoQ. SG&A efficiency was a bright spot, with expenses at 26% of revenue – improved from 29% last year and competitive with peers like Vertex at 25%. Key drivers: - Commercial Infrastructure (45% of SG&A): $55 million supported NP-217, our approved GLP-1/GIP agonist for obesity, capturing 4% U.S. market share post-launch against Eli Lilly's Mounjaro and Novo Nordisk's Wegovy. We optimized our 250-person field force via AI territory mapping, trimming travel costs by 15% while boosting NRx growth to 22% QoQ. - Headcount and Overhead Management: Flat at 1,450 FTEs company-wide, with SG&A headcount down 5% YoY through attrition and offshoring G&A to Ireland, yielding $10 million in savings. Legal and compliance costs rose modestly to $18 million on IP defenses against biosimilar challenges to our legacy TNF inhibitor. - Regional Dynamics: U.S. SG&A was 70% of the total, focused on PBM negotiations amid IRA pricing pressures. Europe saw a 10% sequential dip due to slower NP-217 uptake from NICE reimbursement delays, while ex-U.S. growth markets like Japan contributed positively via our Astellas alliance. Other Operating Expenses: $21 million, or 4% of total OpEx, down 15% YoY. This includes facility costs from our Singapore biologics hub ramp, partially offset by sublease income, and minimal M&A-related amortization.

Our OpEx profile positions AetherNova for sustained mid-teens revenue CAGR through 2027, with R&D-to-SG&A ratio at 1.8x reflecting biotech best practices. We've embedded $50 million in annual run-rate savings from digital twins in manufacturing (inspired by Moderna's playbook) and zero-based budgeting for non-core functions. Looking ahead, Q4 OpEx guidance is $480-500 million, with FY2024 full-year at $1.88-1.92 billion, implying 2-3% below consensus on an adjusted basis. Risks include trial delays from supply chain snarls in ADC payloads – think Daiichi Sankyo's recent experience – and forex headwinds from a stronger USD impacting 15% of spend. Mitigants? Our $1.2 billion cash runway, undrawn $500 million revolver, and pipeline derisking via 40% externalized development.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q3 2024 earnings call. As we dive into the financials, I'd like to spend some time on our R&D expense and pipeline investment priorities, which remain the lifeblood of AetherNova Pharmaceuticals' long-term value creation. In the Pharmaceuticals and Biotech sector, where the average cost to bring a new drug to market exceeds $2.8 billion according to recent Deloitte estimates, disciplined yet aggressive R&D allocation is critical. We're navigating a landscape shaped by the Inflation Reduction Act's pricing reforms, escalating clinical trial costs—up 8-10% annually per IQVIA data—and intensifying competition from Big Pharma players like Pfizer and Roche in oncology and immunology.

Let me start with the numbers. For Q3, our consolidated R&D expense totaled $478 million, representing a 12% year-over-year increase from $427 million in Q3 2023, and up 5% sequentially from Q2. This equates to 38% of our quarterly revenue of $1.26 billion, in line with our peers—think Regeneron's 35-40% range or Vertex's mid-30s—and reflective of our biotech heritage. On a trailing 12-month basis, R&D spend stands at $1.85 billion, or 36% of revenue, with externalized costs (CROs, CMOs, and milestone payments) comprising 55% of the total, up from 50% last year due to accelerated Phase 3 enrollments.

This uptick was driven by three main factors: first, a 15% inflation adjustment in personnel costs for our 1,800-strong R&D workforce, including key hires in computational biology from ex-Google DeepMind talent; second, a $65 million ramp-up in manufacturing scale-up for our lead bispecific antibody, NVB-301, ahead of its PDUFA date in Q2 2025; and third, $42 million in upfront and milestone payments tied to three new strategic partnerships, including our expanded collaboration with Beam Therapeutics on base editing for rare genetic disorders.

Now, turning to our pipeline investment priorities, we're laser-focused on three high-ROI therapeutic areas: oncology (65% of R&D allocation), immunology/rare diseases (25%), and next-gen modalities like gene therapy and ADCs (10%). This mix positions us to capture over $150 billion in addressable markets by 2030, per Evaluate Pharma forecasts, while mitigating binary risks through a diversified 28-asset pipeline—12 in Phase 3 or later, seven in Phase 2/3 readouts next year.

In oncology, our crown jewel, we've allocated $310 million this quarter, up 18% YoY, prioritizing antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) and next-gen TKIs. NVB-301, our HER2-targeted ADC, mirrors the success of Daiichi Sankyo/AstraZeneca's Enhertu with a cleaner safety profile—showing 68% ORR in frontline gastric cancer—and is fully enrolled in the pivotal Phase 3 GALAXY-2 trial across 150 sites in the US, EU, and China. We're also advancing NVB-412, a KRAS G12C inhibitor combo with checkpoint inhibitors, with interim Phase 2 data expected Q1 2025, targeting the $20B+ NSCLC market dominated by Amgen's Lumakras.

Regionally, 40% of our oncology spend is in the US for FDA-aligned trials, 30% in Europe leveraging EMA's PRIME designation for accelerated review—NVB-301 just received it—and 20% in China via our partnership with Innovent Biologics, where trial costs are 30-40% lower and patient recruitment is 2x faster amid the booming local ADC market. This APAC tilt helps offset US site inflation, now at $250K per patient per IQVIA.

In immunology and rare diseases, $120 million was invested, with a spotlight on NVB-567, our IL-4/13 bispecific for atopic dermatitis, posting 75% EASI-75 scores in Phase 2b—competitive with Sanofi's Dupixent—and entering Phase 3 in Q4 with 2,000 patients across North America and Japan. We're also progressing two AAV-based gene therapies: NVB-789 for Pompe disease, in partnership with Sarepta-like logistics for orphan drug status, and a CRISPR-Cas9 candidate for DMD, with IND filing slated for H1 2025. These tap into the $50B rare disease TAM, where pricing power remains robust post-IRA.

Technically, we're embedding AI and machine learning across the board via our NovaAI platform, which has cut hit-to-lead timelines by 40%—from 18 to 11 months—by screening 10 million compounds weekly against our proprietary PROTAC library. This mirrors Schrödinger's physics-based modeling but integrated with wet-lab automation, yielding three new preclinical IO candidates this quarter. We're also investing in multi-omic profiling, partnering with Tempus for real-world evidence to support precision medicine labels, crucial in an era where 60% of new approvals are biomarker-driven per FDA stats.

Strategically, our priorities emphasize derisking through partnerships—$200 million committed this year to alliances like our Beam deal, which includes opt-ins for three more targets—and portfolio pruning: we terminated two early Phase 1 assets last month, saving $30 million annually. Looking forward, we expect full-year 2024 R&D at $1.9-2.0 billion, with Q4 acceleration to support five Phase 3 readouts. This positions AetherNova to deliver 3-5 approvals by 2027, driving peak sales exceeding $15 billion.

We continue to invest in R&D to support our pipeline. Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q2 2024 earnings call for AetherNova Pharmaceuticals Inc. As your CFO, I'll walk you through the key highlights from our balance sheet and cash flow statement, which underscore the financial strength and operational discipline that position us exceptionally well in the dynamic pharmaceuticals and biotech landscape. Our results reflect robust product demand, prudent capital allocation, and strategic investments in our high-potential pipeline—particularly in oncology and rare diseases—amid favorable market tailwinds like the post-COVID recovery in biologics and growing reimbursement for gene therapies.

Let me start with the balance sheet, which remains rock-solid, providing ample liquidity to fuel our innovation engine while maintaining investment-grade metrics. As of September 30, 2024, we ended the quarter with $3.2 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term marketable securities, up 18% sequentially from Q2 and 32% year-over-year. This positions our cash runway at over 4.5 years at current burn rates, even as we accelerate R&D spend—a critical buffer in an industry where Phase III trial delays or FDA adcoms can swing timelines by quarters.

Total assets stood at $12.8 billion, driven by a 12% QoQ increase in intangible assets to $4.1 billion, largely from milestone payments and IP capitalization tied to our next-gen ADC platform, similar to the Seagen acquisition dynamics we saw with Pfizer. Goodwill from last year's $750 million tuck-in acquisition of RareGen Biotech added $1.2 billion, bolstering our rare disease franchise with assets like RGX-501, our AAV gene therapy for homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia.

On the liability side, our net debt improved to $2.1 billion, down from $2.5 billion at year-end 2023, yielding a pristine net debt-to-adjusted EBITDA ratio of 0.8x—well below our 2.0x target and comparable to peers like Regeneron or Vertex. We refinanced $1 billion of our 4.25% senior notes due 2028 at a blended 3.8% rate in April, locking in savings of ~$15 million annually in interest expense. Total debt is $5.3 billion, with 65% fixed-rate and an average maturity of 6.2 years, insulating us from Fed rate volatility.

Working capital metrics are equally strong: Current ratio of 2.4x, up from 2.1x in Q2, supported by DSOs tightening to 58 days from 65 days YoY, thanks to streamlined collections in the U.S. Medicare Part D channel post-Inflation Reduction Act adjustments. Inventory days on hand ticked up modestly to 142 days at 8.2 turns annually, reflecting strategic stockpiling for our Q4 launch of NovaTarget-3, our PD-L1/TIGIT bispecific antibody in NSCLC, akin to Keytruda's supply chain playbook under intense demand.
